F1: The background goroutines take their timeout from the request's `ctx` (`dualwriter_mode3.go:51,110,135,163`), and Go cancels that context once the handler returns, so legacy writes can be cancelled before they finish.
F2: Legacy `Update` now gets the raw `objInfo` instead of an `updateWrapper` holding the storage result, so the playlist legacy storage reruns `UpdatedObject` against its own possibly stale object (`legacy_storage.go:147`) and can end up different from the main storage.
F3: Each write starts its own goroutine with no ordering, so back-to-back create/update/delete calls can reach legacy storage out of order and leave it with wrong data.
F4: In changed code, Create/Update record storage failures as legacy durations, Delete puts `name` in the kind label (unbounded label values), and DeleteCollection records the legacy call as a storage duration, so the metrics are wrong.
